sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Mecklenburg County?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Office of Tax Administration values property and hears appeals, and the Office of the Tax Collector bills and collects. Mecklenburg County sends one bill that covers the county, the City of Charlotte and the six towns of Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Matthews, Mint Hill and Pineville.

The Census Bureau estimated 1,233,383 residents on July 1, 2025, up 10.6 percent from the April 2020 base, spread over 523.61 square miles of land. That density, about 2,130 people per square mile in 2020, is why a single revaluation touches hundreds of thousands of parcels at once. The county said it mailed roughly 449,000 tax bills for 2026.

If your mortgage lender escrows taxes, the real property bill goes to the lender and you receive a notification instead. Sellers with escrow should still confirm with the lender which year has been paid before closing.

sections.h2: When are Mecklenburg County property taxes due, and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and the county lets owners pay through January 5 without interest. For the 2026 bills, the county announced a mailing date of July 28, a due date of September 1, 2026 and an interest-free deadline of January 5, 2027.

Starting January 6, interest of 2 percent applies for January, then 0.75 percent for February and each month after until the bill is paid. State law sets the same pattern in G.S. 105-360.

Mecklenburg County tax calendar, from the county's 2026 bill announcement and G.S. 105-360
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment date for value and ownership
Late JulyBills mailed (July 28 in 2026)
September 1Taxes due and payable
January 5Last day to pay without interest
January 62 percent interest begins
February onward0.75 percent added each month

The county asks anyone who expects trouble paying to call early instead of waiting for the bill to turn delinquent.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Mecklenburg County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail or in person. Online payments by credit or debit card carry a vendor convenience fee, while e-check payments carry none, according to the county.

  • Website: MeckNC.gov/PayTax, using a card or e-check.
  • Phone: toll-free 1-800-994-1026.
  • Mail: the check and the return envelope that came with the bill.
  • In person: the Valerie C. Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, Charlotte, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. Checks go to the Mecklenburg County Tax Collector.

The county warns against online banking bill pay for taxes. A rejected payment cannot have its interest removed, and the funds can take up to four business days to post. For billing questions, the Tax Administration number is 704-336-7600.

sections.h2: What is the 2027 revaluation and how will it change my bill?
sections.html:
Mecklenburg County reappraises every four years, which is more often than the eight-year ceiling in G.S. 105-286. The commissioners set January 1, 2027 as the value date for the next cycle.

A fall 2026 progress report said 428,506 parcels had completed an initial review, with a median increase of about 15 percent for residential property and about 30 percent for commercial. The county said new values and notices are scheduled for early 2027, and that tax rates are set by the city, county and town governing bodies in the spring before bills mail in summer. A higher value does not by itself mean an equal rise in your bill, because the rate can move.

Owners can check the characteristics on their property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov. The county's own example is a house recorded with three bathrooms when it has two, which would inflate value. Fixing a record error before notices go out is cheaper than arguing it later.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mecklenburg County property value?
sections.html:
Appeal to the county Board of Equalization and Review through the Office of Tax Administration. In a revaluation year, appeals cannot be filed until Notices of Value have been mailed, and the notice states a last date to appeal.

In a regular year the filing deadline is the Board's adjournment date, which was May 4, 2026 for the most recent cycle. The county's steps are short:

  • Complete and sign the Formal Appeal Form, then file it by email, by mail to the BER Real Property Appeals address at P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at the Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3500.
  • Send supporting documents with the form or within 45 days of filing it.
  • Expect mailed notice of the hearing roughly 30 days ahead. A continuance request must come within 10 days of that notice.
  • Expect the written decision within 30 days of the hearing.
  • If you disagree, you have 30 days to appeal to the North Carolina Property Tax Commission in Raleigh.

The owner carries the burden of showing the assessed value is wrong and substantially exceeds fair market value. Vehicles and business personal property have their own 30-day appeal windows. Statewide timing rules are in G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290.

sections.h2: What tax relief exists for Mecklenburg County homeowners?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three state programs, and an owner can use only one of them. All are filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not the Department of Revenue.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value of the permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or below $38,800 for 2026 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for income above the limit up to 150 percent of it, for owners who have lived in the home five years. The excess is deferred and becomes due on a transfer (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Mecklenburg and the Town of Davidson also funded the HOMES grant, which paid toward tax bills for qualifying homeowners: up to $650 from the county, with Davidson residents eligible for $534 more. Details and any later rounds are at MeckNC.gov/4Homes.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when I sell a house in Mecklenburg County?
sections.html:
The lien for the year attaches as of January 1, so the bill follows the property into a sale. Under G.S. 105-355, penalties, interest and costs attach on the same date as the lien. An unpaid balance can end in a foreclosure action in Mecklenburg County court.

A seller who closes in the fall may still owe the current-year bill, so the settlement statement should show who covers which months. Ask the Tax Collector for the exact payoff before closing. Recording the deed and paying the excise tax happen at the Register of Deeds, covered on the separate Mecklenburg County deed recording page.

Selling a house with back taxes, a pending appeal or a bill you cannot cover is common. A written cash offer lets you set the closing date around the tax calendar.

faqs.q: Is the Mecklenburg County tax bill due September 1 or January 5?
faqs.a: Both dates matter. The bill is due September 1, and the county lets you pay through January 5 without interest. Starting January 6, 2 percent interest applies, then 0.75 percent for each later month.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my value right after the 2027 revaluation notice arrives?
faqs.a: Yes, but only after notices are mailed. The notice lists a last date to appeal, and the formal appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and Review. Include your evidence with the form or within 45 days of filing it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Mecklenburg County property taxes in person?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector's counter is at the Valerie C. Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, Charlotte, open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. It accepts cash, cards, money orders and checks made out to the Mecklenburg County Tax Collector.

faqs.q: Does a revaluation raise my tax bill by the same percent as my value?
faqs.a: No. The bill is the assessed value times the tax rate, and the city, county and town governments set rates in the spring after new values are posted. Owners should compare the new value and the adopted rates before judging the bill.

faqs.q: Can I get a property tax break if I am over 65 in Mecklenburg County?
faqs.a: Possibly. The state elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value for owners 65 or older with income at or below $38,800 for 2026. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, and remember you may use only one of the three state programs.
